paragraphs: John Marshall Bancorp, Inc. was organized as a Virginia corporation in 2016 to serve as the holding company for John Marshall Bank. The Company and the Bank are each headquartered in Reston, Virginia (approximately 20 miles west of Washington, D.C.). The Company commenced operations as a bank holding company on March 1, 2017 following a reorganization transaction in which it became the Bank's holding company. This transaction was treated as an internal reorganization as all shareholders of the Bank became shareholders of the Company. As a bank holding company, the Company is subject to regulation and supervision by the Federal Reserve. The Company has no material operations other than its sole ownership of the Bank. The Bank is a Virginia chartered commercial bank that commenced operations in 2006. The Bank is supervised and regulated by the Federal Reserve and the Bureau of Financial Institutions of the Virginia State Corporation Commission (the "Virginia BFI").

We primarily serve small to medium-sized businesses, their owners and employees, professional corporations, non-profits and individuals with a broad range of banking products and financial services. Some of the products and services that we offer include commercial checking, savings and money market accounts, certificates of deposit, treasury and cash management services, commercial and industrial loans, commercial real estate loans, residential and commercial construction and development loans, U.S. Small Business Administration ("SBA") 7(a) loans, consumer mortgages, online banking, and mobile banking. As of December 31, 2025, we had total consolidated assets of $2.33 billion, gross loans of $1.97 billion, total deposits of $1.97 billion and total shareholders' equity of $265.6 million.

A key factor in our ability to achieve our strategic goals and create shareholder value is the attractiveness of our market area. The market area in which we operate has seen considerable population and economic growth over the past several decades. Recent economic data suggest that the relative economic strength of our market area will continue, enabling us to grow our customer base and find opportunities to grow our market share.

The Bank's primary service area includes Arlington, Fairfax, Loudoun and Prince William counties in Virginia, Montgomery County in Maryland and the District of Columbia. The Bank has eight full service branch offices located in these contiguous cities or counties.

Our primary service area comprises the majority of the population and household income of the Washington-Arlington-Alexandria, DC-VA-MD-WV ("Washington, D.C.") Metropolitan Statistical Area ("MSA"). The Washington, D.C. MSA, according to U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis data, ranked sixth among all MSAs for 2023 gross domestic product. According to data sourced from S&P Global Market Intelligence, among the largest MSAs ranked by gross domestic product (New York, Los Angeles, Chicago, San Francisco, Dallas and Washington), the Washington, D.C. MSA ranked second for 2025 median household income at $123,209, second in 2026 to 2031 projected population growth at 2.8% and first in the percentage of inhabitants 25 or older with a bachelor's degree or higher educational attainment at 55.4%. According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, the Washington, D.C. MSA's December 2025 unemployment rate was 4.5%, less than the average of six largest MSAs.

Based upon Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (the "FDIC") data as of June 30, 2025, the Washington D.C. MSA housed $315 billion of deposits, with the top five financial institutions controlling 68%. At June 30, 2025, our deposits were $1.90 billion, ranked 17th in the MSA and represented a 0.6% market share. Nine of the sixteen banks ranked ahead of the Company are headquartered outside of the Washington, D.C. MSA. Our market area has experienced a significant degree of banking consolidation over the last several decades. Since the Company's inception, banking assets in excess of $55 billion have been acquired. We believe that as financial institutions are merged with or acquired by remote, larger institutions, their customers can become further removed from the point of decision making. The consolidation trend provides an opportunity for the Company to execute a focused strategy of offering personalized services to attract potential customers who are underserved or dissatisfied.

Given the Company's proximity to Washington, D.C., the federal government has contributed to the growth and generally played a stabilizing role in our market area's economy. In recent years, local governments have made great strides in diversifying their local economies. Virginia Tech selected the City of Alexandria as the site for its innovation campus which aims to graduate 25,000 new bachelor's and master's students in computer science and related fields over the next 20 years. The innovation campus opened February 28, 2025. The $1 billion, 600,000 square foot campus is expected to confer over 600 graduate degrees annually and provide talent to spur further technological growth. By 2030, Amazon's headquarters in Arlington County is expected to occupy at least four million square feet of office space. Phase one of Amazon's HQ2 was completed in the spring 2023. Amazon will invest more than $2 billion to establish its new headquarters, which will create at least 25,000 high-wage jobs by 2030. Fairfax County is home to ten Fortune 500 company headquarters and 17 Fortune 1000 company headquarters. Loudoun County is known as "data center alley" as it has the world's highest concentration of data centers with more than 30 million square feet of data center space. Loudoun County is home to more than 3,500 technology companies. Prince William County has partnered with George Mason University to found the Prince William Science Accelerator, a fast-growing biotechnology cluster to foster the study of life sciences.

We believe the size, growth, economic diversity and banking consolidation within the Washington, D.C. MSA, when combined with our business strategy, provide us with excellent opportunities for long-term, sustainable growth.
We believe that we are well-positioned to execute our banking strategy as a result of our competitive strengths:

● Experienced management team. Our executive management team brings decades of in-market experience. Christopher W. Bergstrom, our President and Chief Executive Officer, has a banking career spanning nearly 44 years. Mr. Bergstrom joined the Company in 2018. Prior to joining the Company, Mr. Bergstrom served in executive management capacities at banks in our market area that were significantly larger than the Company. Andrew J. Peden, our Chief Banking Officer, has over 25 years of banking experience, all of it in the Washington, D.C. MSA. He joined the Company in 2018. Kent D. Carstater, our Chief Financial Officer, has over 28 years of financial services experience as a commercial banker and investment banker. He joined the Company in 2016. Jason R. McDonough, our Chief Lending Officer, has close to 20 years of banking experience, all of it in the Washington, D.C. MSA. He joined the Company in 2018. Messrs. Bergstrom, Peden, Carstater, and McDonough have deepened the management team by recruiting experienced financial services professionals who have demonstrated their ability to drive organic growth, improve operating efficiencies and establish a robust risk management framework.

● Disciplined credit culture. In originating loans, our relationship managers focus on experienced business owners with demonstrated capacity to fulfill their financial obligations. Loan officers have relatively low individual discretionary loan authority levels, which generally results in loan committee vetting to uphold appropriate structure and terms prior to approval. Loan committee meetings are held regularly and on an as-needed basis to promote prompt decisions. We utilize an independent, regionally based loan review firm, that focuses exclusively on community and regional banks, to validate our risk ratings and assess our underwriting and loan administration. We believe that our rigorous underwriting and diligent monitoring of the loan portfolio have created a "credit first" mentality that permeates the Company and is reflected in our asset quality statistics. As of December 31, 2025, the Company had no non-accrual loans and no other real estate owned ("OREO"). In each of the past five fiscal years, net charge-offs have not exceeded 0.02% of average gross loans.

● Conservative balance sheet. The Company's balance sheet provides the foundation for prudent growth. The Bank's capital ratios exceed the thresholds required of a well-capitalized institution. As of December 31, 2025, the Bank had the capacity to add $1.0 billion of risk-weighted assets to its balance sheet and still maintain well-capitalized status. The Company has ample liquidity to meet its obligations and fund anticipated loan growth. As of December 31, 2025, the Bank had over $233.5 million of liquid assets, defined as cash and unpledged securities, over $594 million of available secured borrowing facilities and $110 million of available unsecured borrowing facilities. Management believes the Company's balance sheet is well-positioned for organic growth and potential acquisitions.

● Proven ability to grow. Over the long term we have demonstrated an ability to grow our loans and deposits. For the eight year period ended December 31, 2025, the Company's compound annual growth rates in assets, gross loans, deposits and non-interest bearing deposits were 8.9%, 8.8%, 10.4% and 12.0%, respectively. Our team of professionals has been an important driver of our organic growth by developing banking relationships with current and potential customers. We believe our ability to recruit and retain talented, customer service-oriented professionals has been at the core of our growing and expanding banking relationships.

● Accelerating earnings momentum and completive returns. The Company reported net income of $21.2 million for the twelve months ended December 31, 2025, a 24.0% increase over the $17.1 million reported for the twelve months ended December 31, 2024. Net income for the fourth quarter of 2025 marked the sixth consecutive quarter of net income growth. From December 31, 2024 to December 31, 2025, the Company increased book value per share from $17.28 to $18.69. In addition to the $0.30 per share cash dividend paid in July 2025, total return to shareholders when considering the change in book value per share and cash dividend for 2025 was $1.71 per share, an increase of 9.9%.

headings: Risks Related to Our Lending Activities
We may not be able to measure and limit our credit risk adequately, which could adversely affect our profitability.
Our allowance for loan credit losses may be inadequate to absorb expected losses inherent in the loan portfolio.
If our non-performing assets increase, our earnings will be adversely affected.
Our focus on lending to small to medium-sized businesses may increase our credit risk.

We are exposed to higher credit risk by commercial real estate, commercial and industrial and construction and development-based lending as well as relationship exposure with a number of large borrowers.
A significant percentage of our loans are attributable to a relatively small number of borrowers.
Lack of seasoning of our loan portfolio could increase risk of credit defaults in the future.
The appraisals and other valuation techniques we use in evaluating and monitoring loans secured by real property and other real estate owned may not accurately reflect the net value of the asset.
Risks Related to Funding and Liquidity
Our deposit portfolio includes significant concentrations and a large percentage of our deposits are attributable to a relatively small number of customers.
Limits on our ability to use brokered deposits as part of our funding strategy may adversely affect our ability to grow.
Liquidity risk could impair our ability to fund operations and meet our obligations as they become due.
The proportion of our deposit account balances that exceed FDIC insurance limits may expose the Bank to enhanced liquidity risk in times of financial distress.
Unrealized losses in our securities portfolio could affect liquidity.
Risks Related to Our Business, Industry and Markets
We operate in a highly competitive market and face increasing competition from a variety of traditional and new financial services providers.
Failure to keep up with the rapid technological changes in the financial services industry could have an adverse effect on our competitive position and profitability.
Interest rate shifts may reduce net interest income and otherwise negatively impact our financial condition and results of operations.
The fair value of our investment securities can fluctuate due to factors outside of our control.
Inflation can have an adverse impact on our business and on our customers.
Monetary policies and regulations of the Federal Reserve could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.
We are subject to certain operational risks, including, but not limited to, customer or employee fraud and data processing system failures and errors.
We rely on third parties to provide key components of our business infrastructure.

We follow a relationship-based operating model and our ability to maintain our reputation is critical to the success of our business and the failure to do so may materially adversely affect our performance.
We may be adversely affected by the lack of soundness of other financial institutions or market utilities.
External and internal risk has proliferated in recent years.
Our risk management framework may not be effective in mitigating risks and/or losses to us.

System failure or breaches of our network security, including as a result of cyber-attacks or data security breaches, could subject us to increased operating costs as well as litigation and other liabilities.

The Company's business continuity plans or data security systems could prove to be inadequate, resulting in a material interruption in, or disruption to, its business and a negative impact on results of operations.
We are dependent on the use of data and modeling in both our management's decision-making generally and in meeting regulatory expectations in particular.
We are exposed to risk of environmental liabilities with respect to properties to which we obtain title.
Risks Related to our Regulatory Environment
Our industry is highly regulated, and the regulatory framework, together with any future legislative or regulatory changes, may have a materially adverse effect on our operations.
We are subject to stringent capital requirements, which could have an adverse effect on our operations.
paragraphs: In addition to the other information set forth in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including the information addressed under "Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" and "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations," and our consolidated financial statements and the related notes, you should carefully consider the factors discussed below. These factors could adversely affect our future business, financial condition, liquidity and results of operations, and could cause our actual results to differ materially from our historical results or the results contemplated by the forward-looking statements contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, in which case the trading price of our common stock could decline. Our business, financial condition, liquidity or results of operations could also be harmed by risks and uncertainties not currently known to us or that we currently do not believe are material. References to past events in these risk factors are provided by way of example only and are not intended to be a complete listing or a representation as to whether or not such factors have occurred in the past or their likelihood of occurring in the future.

Our business depends on our ability to successfully measure and manage credit risk. As a lender, we are exposed to the risk that the principal of, or interest on, a loan will not be paid timely or at all or that the value of any collateral supporting a loan will be insufficient to cover our outstanding exposure. In addition, we are exposed to risks with respect to the period of time over which the loan may be repaid, risks relating to proper loan underwriting, risks resulting from changes in economic and industry conditions, and risks inherent in dealing with individual loans and borrowers. The creditworthiness of a borrower is affected by many factors, including local market conditions and general economic conditions. Many of our loans are made to small to medium-sized businesses that are less able to withstand competitive, economic and financial pressures than larger borrowers. If the overall economic climate in the United States, generally, or in our market specifically, experiences material disruption, our borrowers may experience difficulties in repaying their loans, the collateral we hold may decrease in value or become illiquid, and the level of nonperforming loans, charge-offs and delinquencies could rise and require significant additional provisions for loan credit losses. Additional factors related to the credit quality of multifamily residential, real estate construction and other commercial real estate loans include the quality of management of the business and tenant vacancy rates.

Our risk management practices, such as monitoring the concentration of our loans within specific markets and our credit approval, review and administrative practices, may not adequately reduce credit risk, and our credit administration personnel, policies and procedures may not adequately adapt to changes in economic or any other conditions affecting customers and the quality of the loan portfolio. A failure to effectively measure and limit the credit risk associated with our loan portfolio may result in loan defaults, foreclosures and additional charge-offs, and may necessitate that we significantly increase our allowance for loan credit losses, each of which could adversely affect our net income. As a result, our inability to successfully manage credit risk could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

Experience in the banking industry indicates that a portion of our loans will become delinquent, and that some may only be partially repaid or may never be repaid at all. We may experience losses for reasons beyond our control, such as the impact of general economic conditions on customers and their businesses. Accordingly, we maintain an allowance for loan credit losses that represents management's judgment of expected losses and risks inherent in our loan portfolio. In determining the size of our allowance for loan credit losses, we rely on an analysis of our loan portfolio considering historical loss experience, volume and types of loans, trends in classification, volume and trends in delinquencies and nonaccruals, economic conditions and other pertinent information. The determination of the appropriate level of the allowance for loan credit losses is inherently highly subjective and requires us to use significant judgment to estimate the level of credit risk and expected losses of the institution based on an evaluation the factors and circumstances that exist as of the applicable measurement date, all of which may change materially. Although we endeavor to maintain our allowance for loan credit losses at a level adequate to absorb any inherent expected losses in the loan portfolio, these estimates of

loan credit losses are necessarily subjective and their accuracy depends on the outcome of future events. As of December 31, 2025, the allowance for loan credit losses was $19.8 million or 1.00% of total loans, net of unearned income.

Deterioration of economic conditions affecting borrowers, new information regarding existing loans, inaccurate management assumptions, identification of additional problem loans, temporary modifications, loan forgiveness, automatic forbearance and other factors, both within and outside of our control, may result in our experiencing higher levels of nonperforming assets and charge-offs, and incurring loan credit losses in excess of our current allowance for loan credit losses, requiring us to make material additions to our allowance for loan credit losses, which could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis of the consolidated financial condition and results of operations of the Company and its subsidiary should be read in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements and related notes presented in Item 8, Financial Statements and Supplementary Data, of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Historical results of operations and the percentage relationships among any amounts included, and any trends that may appear, may not be indicative of results of operations or trends in operations for any future periods.

This discussion and analysis contains financial information determined by methods other than in accordance with GAAP. Management believes that the supplemental non-GAAP information provides a better comparison of period-to-period operating performance. Additionally, the Company believes this information is utilized by regulators and market analysts to evaluate a company's financial condition and therefore, such information is useful to investors. Non-GAAP measures used in this report consist of tax-equivalent net interest income and net interest margin.

These disclosures should not be viewed as a substitute for financial results in accordance with GAAP, nor are they necessarily comparable to non-GAAP performance measures which may be presented by other companies. Where the non-GAAP financial measure is used, the comparable GAAP financial measure, as well as reconciliation to that comparable GAAP financial measure, a statement of the company's reasons for utilizing the non-GAAP financial measure, can be found within this discussion and analysis.

John Marshall Bancorp, Inc. is a bank holding company headquartered in Reston, Virginia primarily serving the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area. The material business operations of the Company are performed through its only subsidiary, John Marshall Bank. As a result, the discussion and analysis within this section primarily relate to activities conducted at the Bank.

As with most community banks, the Bank derives a significant portion of its income from interest received on loans and investments. The Bank's primary source of funding is deposits, both interest-bearing and non-interest-bearing. To account for credit risk inherent in all loans, the Bank maintains an allowance for loan credit losses to absorb lifetime losses on existing loans. The Bank establishes and maintains this allowance by recording a provision for loan credit losses against earnings. In addition to net interest income, the Bank also generates income through service charges on deposits, insurance commission income, merchant services fee income, swap fee income and gain on sale of the guaranteed portion of U.S. Small Business Administration ("SBA") 7(a) loans.

Net income for the year ended December 31, 2025 was $21.2 million ($1.49 per diluted common share) compared to $17.1 million ($1.20 per diluted common share) for the year ended December 31, 2024, representing a 24.0% and 24.2% increase in net income and earnings per diluted common share, respectively. The increase during 2025 was driven by a $9.5 million increase in net interest income, which was partially offset by a $2.1 million increase in provision for credit losses and a $1.8 million increase in non-interest expense. The increase in net interest income was driven primarily by the decrease in

rates of interest-bearing deposits coupled with increases in average balances and yields of the loan portfolio. The net interest margin for the twelve months ended December 31, 2025 was 2.68% as compared to 2.28% for the same period in the prior year. An improvement in net interest margin during the current year was attributable to management's proactive approach in repricing deposits concurrently with each of the three federal funds rate cuts totaling 75 basis points since September 2025 through December 2025. Higher provision for credit losses during the twelve months ended December 31, 2025 was primarily a result of the growth in the loan portfolio and the related changes in the portfolio mix, coupled with the impact of the charge-off of the unguaranteed portion of one commercial business SBA 7(a) loan during the fourth quarter of 2025 and management's assessment of the qualitative adjustments reflecting changing local economic conditions monitored throughout the year. An increase in non-interest expense during the current year as compared to the prior year was primarily attributable to an increase in salaries and employee benefits, which was mainly associated with the higher headcount within the Company and an increase in incentive compensation tied to the Company's operating performance. The investments made to expand the headcount during the current year are expected to contribute to the future growth of the Company and subsequent increases in revenues. The increase in incentive compensation reflected the 24% year-over-year increase in net income and the fact that the Company's operating performance for 2025 exceeded the budget and strategic plan.
The results for 2025 reflect the following:
● At December 31, 2025, total assets were $2.33 billion, a 4.4% increase compared to $2.23 billion at December 31, 2024.

● Total loans, net of unearned income, increased by $103.2 million or 5.5% to $1.98 billion at December 31, 2025 compared to $1.87 billion at December 31, 2024. The increase in loans from December 31, 2025, was primarily attributable to growth in construction & development loans and residential mortgage loans, partially offset by a decline in commercial owner-occupied real estate loans. All other portfolios remained relatively unchanged during the most recent year.

● Deposits increased by $79.9 million or 4.2% to $1.97 billion at December 31, 2025 compared to $1.89 billion at December 31, 2024. During the year, interest-bearing deposits increased by $80.4 million or 5.5%, while non-interest bearing deposits remained relatively unchanged. Growth in interest-bearing deposits during the current year was driven by core time deposits, interest-bearing demand deposits and money market accounts, which increased by $24.5 million, $24.2 million and $16.0 million, respectively.

● Net interest income for 2025 increased $9.5 million or 18.6% compared to 2024. The declining interest rate environment during the current year resulted in a $6.4 million decrease in interest expense, while interest income grew by $3.1 million.

● The net interest margin for 2025 was 2.68% compared to 2.28% for 2024. An expansion of the net interest margin for the current year reflects the lower rate paid on interest-bearing liabilities in combination with a higher yield on interest-earning assets. As compared to the prior year, the rate paid on interest-bearing liabilities declined by 41 basis points, while the yield on interest-earning assets rose 10 basis points, resulting in a net interest margin expansion of 40 basis points.

● The provision for credit losses for 2025 amounted to a charge of $1.7 million as compared to a $0.4 million recovery of a provision for credit losses for 2024. The provision for credit losses for 2025 was mainly a reflection of growth of the loan portfolio and the related changes in the portfolio mix along with the management's assessment of the qualitative adjustments reflecting changing economic conditions and portfolio concentrations monitored throughout the year.

paragraphs: John Marshall Bancorp, Inc. 於 2016 年在維吉尼亞州設立為一家公司，作為 John Marshall Bank 的控股公司。本公司與銀行皆位於維吉尼亞州 Reston（約距離華盛頓特區西北方 20 英里）。本公司於 2017 年 3 月 1 日開始運作，成為銀行的控股公司，此交易為一內部重組，所有銀行股東皆成為本公司股東。作為銀行控股公司，本公司受美國聯邦儲備銀行監管。本公司除擁有銀行外，無其他重大營運。銀行為一維吉尼亞州核准的商業銀行，於 2006 年開始營運。銀行受美國聯邦儲備銀行與維吉尼亞州公司委員會財務機構局（"維吉尼亞 BFI"）監督與管理。

本公司主要服務中小型企業、其所有者及員工、專業會計事務所、非營利機構及個人，提供廣泛的銀行產品與金融服務。我們所提供的部分產品與服務包括商業支票帳戶、儲蓄與貨幣市場帳戶、定期存款、國庫與現金管理服務、商業與工業貸款、商業不動產貸款、住宅與商業建設與開發貸款、美國小企業管理局（"SBA"）7(a)貸款、消費者房貸、網際網路銀行服務及行動銀行服務。截至2025年12月31日，本公司總合併資產為2.33 十億美元，總放款額為1.97 十億美元，總存款額為1.97 十億美元，總股東權益為265.6 百萬美元。
我們實現戰略目標與創造股東價值的能力，關鍵在於我們市場區域的吸引力。我們所處的市場區域過去數十年來經歷了相當的人口與經濟成長。近期經濟數據顯示，我們市場區域相對經濟強勢將持續，使我們能擴大客戶基礎，並尋找擴大市場佔有率的機會。
銀行的主要服務區域包括維吉尼亞州的阿靈頓、費爾法克斯、路易斯堡與普林斯威廉縣，馬裏蘭州的蒙哥馬利縣，以及華盛頓特區。銀行在這些連續的城市或縣市設有八家全功能分行。

我們的主要服務區域涵蓋華盛頓-阿靈頓-亞歷山德里亞，DC-VA-MD-WV（"華盛頓特區"）都會區（"MSA"）的大多數人口與家庭收入。根據美國經濟分析局數據，華盛頓特區 MSA 在 2023 年的國內生產總值（GDP）排名第六。根據 S&P 全球市場智慧數據，於美國最大都會區中按 GDP 排名（紐約、洛杉磯、芝加哥、舊金山、達拉斯與華盛頓），華盛頓特區 MSA 在 2025 年家庭收入中位數為 123,209 美元，排名第二；在 2026 至 2031 年預測人口成長中排名第二，成長率為 2.8%；在 25 歲以上居民擁有大學學位或更高教育程度的比例中排名第一，為 55.4%。根據美國勞工統計局數據，華盛頓特區 MSA 在 2025 年 12 月的失業率為 4.5%，低於六大最大都會區的平均值。

根據美國聯邦存款保險公司（Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation，簡稱 FDIC）截至 2025 年 6 月 30 日的資料，華盛頓特區都會區（Washington D.C. MSA）存放款金額為 315 十億美元，前五大金融機構掌握 68%。截至 2025 年 6 月 30 日，本公司存放款金額為 1.90 十億美元，在都會區排名第 17 名，佔市場佔有率 0.6%。十六家銀行中，有九家排名在本公司之前，其總部位於華盛頓特區都會區以外。本公司所處的市場區域在過去數十年來經歷了相當程度的銀行合併。自本公司成立以來，已取得銀行資產超過 55 十億美元。我們認為，當金融機構與遠處的大型機構合併或被收購時，其客戶可能更遠離決策點。此合併趨勢為本公司執行專注於提供個性化服務的策略，以吸引未被充分服務或不滿意的潛在客戶，提供了機會。

本公司位於華盛頓特區附近，聯邦政府對當地經濟的成長有所貢獻，並通常在本市場區域的經濟中扮演穩定角色。近年來，當地政府在多元化地方經濟方面已取得重大進展。維吉尼亞理工大學選定亞歷山德里亞市作為創新校區的所在地，該校區旨在未來二十年內培養25,000名電腦科學及相關領域的學士及碩士學生。創新校區於2025年2月28日開幕。該校區預計投資1十億美元，總面積為600,000平方英呎，預計每年可頒發超過600個研究生學位，並提供人才以促進進一步的科技成長。至2030年，亞馬遜在阿靈頓縣的總部預計將佔用至少四百萬平方英呎的辦公空間。亞馬遜總部第二階段（HQ2）的第一期工程於2023年春季完成。亞馬遜將投資超過2十億美元以建立其新總部，預計至2030年將創造至少25,000個高薪工作機會。費爾法克斯縣擁有十家《財富》500大公司的總部及17家《財富》1000大公司的總部。路易維爾縣以「資料中心走廊」聞名，因其擁有全球最高的資料中心密度，資料中心空間超過30百萬平方英呎。路易維爾縣擁有超過3,500家科技公司。普林斯威廉縣與喬治梅森大學合作成立普林斯威廉科學加速器，是一個快速成長的生物科技集羣，以促進生命科學的研究。
我們相信，華盛頓特區 MSA 的規模、成長、經濟多樣性與銀行合併現象，結合我們的商業策略，為我們提供長遠且可持續成長的優良機會。
我們相信我們已具備執行銀行策略的優勢，這是因為我們的競爭優勢：

● 有經驗的管理團隊。我們的高階管理團隊擁有數十年的市場經驗。Christopher W. Bergstrom，本公司董事長兼首席執行官，擁有近44年的銀行業經驗。Bergstrom先生於2018年加入本公司。在加入本公司之前，Bergstrom先生曾在市場區內規模遠大於本公司的銀行擔任高階管理職務。Andrew J. Peden，本公司首席銀行官，擁有超過25年的銀行經驗，全部都在華盛頓特區都會區（Washington, D.C. MSA）。他於2018年加入本公司。Kent D. Carstater，本公司首席財務官，擁有超過28年的金融服務經驗，作為商業銀行家和投資銀行家。他於2016年加入本公司。Jason R. McDonough，本公司首席貸款官，擁有近20年的銀行經驗，全部都在華盛頓特區都會區（Washington, D.C. MSA）。他於2018年加入本公司。Bergstrom、Peden、Carstater和McDonough先生透過招募有經驗的金融服務專業人士，深化了管理團隊，這些專業人士已展現其推動內生性成長、改善營運效率及建立強固風險管理架構的能力。

● 責任至上的信貸文化。在發放貸款時，我們的關係經理專注於有經驗的企業所有者，這些所有者已展現出履行財務義務的能力。貸款經理的個人貸款授權水平相對較低，這通常導致貸款委員會審查以確保貸款結構和條款適當，再進行批准。貸款委員會會議定期舉行，並在需要時舉行以促進迅速決策。我們使用一家獨立的、區域性的貸款審查機構，專注於社區銀行和區域銀行，以驗證我們的風險評級並評估我們的貸款審批及貸款管理。我們相信我們嚴謹的貸款審批及對貸款組合的勤勉監測，已創造出一種「信貸為先」的思維方式，這種思維方式滲透於本公司，並反映在我們的資產品質統計資料中。截至2025年12月31日，本公司沒有未計息貸款，也沒有其他實質資產（"OREO"）。在過去五個財務年度中，淨核銷金額均未超過平均貸款總額的0.02%。

● 健全的資產負債表。本公司的資產負債表為審慎成長奠定了基礎。銀行的資本比率超過資本充足機構所需的門檻。截至2025年12月31日，銀行可增加10億美元的風險加權資產至其資產負債表，同時仍維持資本充足狀態。本公司擁有充足的流動性以履行其義務並資助預期的貸款成長。截至2025年12月31日，銀行擁有超過233.5百萬美元的流動資產，定義為現金及未質押證券，超過594百萬美元的可用擔保融資設施，以及110百萬美元的可用無擔保融資設施。管理層認為本公司的資產負債表已具備內生性成長及潛在收購的優勢。
● 證明的成長能力。長期而言，我們已展現出成長貸款和存款的能力。截至2025年12月31日的八個財務年度期間，本公司資產、貸款總額、存款及非利息存款的複合年成長率分別為8.9%、8.8%、10.4%及12.0%。我們的專業團隊在發展與現有及潛在客戶的銀行關係方面發揮了重要作用。我們相信我們招募及留住具才能且以客戶服務為導向的專業人才的能力，是我們銀行關係成長與擴張的核心。

● 加速的獲利動能與競爭性回報。本公司於2025年12月31日的十二個月內報告淨收入為21.2百萬美元，較2024年12月31日的17.1百萬美元成長24.0%。2025年第四季的淨收入標誌著連續第六個季度的淨收入成長。從2024年12月31日至2025年12月31日，本公司每股帳面價值從17.28美元增至18.69美元。除了2025年7月支付的每股0.30美元現金股息外，考慮到2025年帳面價值每股變動及現金股息，總回報每股為1.71美元，成長9.9%。

paragraphs: 以下對本公司及其子公司整體財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析，應配合本年度10-K表報中第8項「財務報表與補充資料」所列之整體財務報表及其相關附註一併閱讀。歷史營運成果與任何數值之間的百分比關係，以及可能出現之趨勢，未必能反映未來任何期間之營運成果或營運趨勢。
本討論與分析包含依循一般會計準則（GAAP）以外之方法所確定之財務資訊。管理階層認為，補充之非GAAP財務資訊能提供更佳之期間對期間營運表現比較。此外，本公司認為此資訊被監管機構與市場分析師用以評估公司之財務狀況，因此對投資人而言此資訊具備參考價值。本報告所使用之非GAAP衡量指標包含稅後等效淨利息收入與淨利息邊際。
這些揭露資訊不應視為依循一般會計準則（GAAP）財務結果之替代，亦未必與其他公司所呈現之非GAAP財務衡量指標具有可比性。於使用非GAAP財務指標時，可對應之GAAP財務指標，以及該可對應GAAP財務指標之調整說明，均可於本討論與分析中找到。
John Marshall Bancorp, Inc. 為一銀行控股公司，總部設於維吉尼亞州Reston，主要服務華盛頓特區都會區。本公司之主要業務運作均透過其唯一子公司John Marshall Bank執行。因此，本節之討論與分析主要與銀行之營運活動相關。

如同大多數社區銀行，本行收入的大部分來自貸款及投資所收取的利息。本行的主要資金來源為存款，包括有息存款與無息存款。為應對所有貸款內含的信用風險，本行維持一個貸款信用損失備抵準備金，以吸收現有貸款的終身損失。本行透過將貸款信用損失備抵準備金計入營業收入，來建立並維持此準備金。除了淨利息收入外，本行亦透過存款服務費收入、保險佣金收入、商家服務費收入、掉期費收入以及銷售美國小企業管理局（"SBA"）7(a)貸款擔保部分的獲利來產生收入。

2025年12月31日財年淨收入為21.2 百萬美元（每股稀釋普通股1.49美元），與2024年12月31日財年淨收入17.1 百萬美元（每股稀釋普通股1.20美元）相比，淨收入與每股稀釋普通股 earnings 分別成長24.0%與24.2%。2025年的成長主要來自淨利息收入增加9.5 百萬美元，此成長部分抵銷了信用損失備抵準備金增加2.1 百萬美元與非利息費用增加1.8 百萬美元。淨利息收入的成長主要來自於有息存款利率的下降，同時貸款組合的平均餘額與收益率增加。

2025年12月31日財年淨利息邊際為2.68%，與前一年同期2.28%相比。本年淨利息邊際的改善歸因於管理層在每次聯邦基金利率下降75個基點（自2025年9月至2025年12月）時，積極重新評估存款利率。2025年12月31日財年信用損失備抵準備金增加，主要是由於貸款組合成長與相關組合結構的變化，同時也受到2025年第四季一筆商業企業SBA 7(a)貸款未擔保部分核銷的影響，以及管理層對當地經濟條件變動的質化調整評估。本年非利息費用增加，主要是因為薪資與員工福利增加，這與公司內高層人數增加以及與公司營運表現掛鉤的激勵報酬增加有關。本年為擴充人力所進行的投資，預期將有助於公司未來的成長與隨之而來的收入增加。激勵報酬的增加反映了淨收入較去年同期成長24%，且公司2025年營運表現超越預算與戰略計畫。
2025年的結果反映以下內容：
● 2025年12月31日，總資產為2.33十億美元，較2024年12月31日的2.23十億美元成長4.4%。
● 經扣除未實現收入後的總貸款餘額，較2024年12月31日的1.87十億美元增加103.2百萬美元或5.5%，至2025年12月31日的1.98十億美元。貸款餘額較2025年12月31日成長，主要係因建設及開發貸款與住宅房貸貸款成長，部分抵銷商業所有權佔用不動產貸款減少的影響。其他資產組合在最近一年內維持相對不變。
● 存款餘額較2024年12月31日的1.89十億美元增加79.9百萬美元或4.2%，至2025年12月31日的1.97十億美元。本年度，計息存款餘額增加80.4百萬美元或5.5%，而非計息存款餘額維持相對不變。本年度計息存款成長，主要係因核心定期存款、計息活期存款及貨幣市場帳戶增加24.5百萬美元、24.2百萬美元及16.0百萬美元。
● 2025年淨利息收入較2024年增加9.5百萬美元或18.6%。本年度利率下降的環境導致利息支出減少6.4百萬美元，同時利息收入增加3.1百萬美元。
● 2025年淨利息 margin 為2.68%，較2024年的2.28%成長。本年度淨利息 margin 的擴張反映於利息負債支付利率下降，以及利息資產收益率上升。與前一年相比，利息負債支付利率下降41個基點，而利息資產收益率上升10個基點，導致淨利息 margin 擴張40個基點。
● 2025年信貸減損提撥為1.7百萬美元的費用，較2024年0.4百萬美元的信貸減損提撥回復金額。2025年信貸減損提撥主要反映貸款組合成長及相關組合結構變動，以及管理層對經濟環境變動及組合集中度的質化調整評估，並於本年度持續監測。

headings: 與我們貸款業務相關的風險
我們可能無法充分衡量並控制信用風險，這可能會對我們的獲利造成不利影響。
我們的貸款信用損失撥備可能不足以吸收貸款組閤中固有的預期損失。
若我們的不良資產增加，將會對我們的獲利造成不利影響。
我們專注於對中小型企業的貸款，可能會增加我們的信用風險。
我們因商業不動產、商業及工業貸款以及建設與開發相關貸款，以及與多數大型借款人的關係，而面臨較高的信用風險。
我們貸款組閤中相當大的比例來自相對較少的借款人。
我們貸款組合的成熟度不足，可能會增加未來信用違約的風險。
我們用來評估及監控以不動產為抵押品貸款及其他不動產所有權之技術與評價方法，可能無法準確反映資產之淨價值。
與資金及流動性相關之風險
本公司存款組合包含重大集中度，且本公司存款之大部分歸屬於相對較少數之客戶。
本公司運用經紀存款作為資金策略之能力受到限制，可能不利於本公司之成長。
流動性風險可能影響本公司資金營運及履行到期義務之能力。
本公司存款帳戶餘額超過FDIC保險上限之比例，可能在財務危機時期使銀行面臨更高之流動性風險。
本公司證券組閤中未實現之損失可能影響流動性。
與本公司業務、產業及市場相關之風險
我們所處的市場為高度競爭，並面臨來自多種傳統及新興金融服務提供者的競爭壓力。
若無法跟上金融服務業快速的技術變革，將可能對我們的競爭地位及獲利能力產生不利影響。
利率變動可能降低我們的淨利息收入，並以其他方式對我們的財務狀況及營運成果產生負面影響。
我們的投資證券公允價值可能因我們無法控制的因素而波動。
通貨膨脹可能對我們的業務及客戶產生不利影響。
聯邦儲備系統的貨幣政策及規範可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
與我們營運相關的風險
我們面臨某些營運風險，包括但不限於客戶或員工詐欺及資料處理系統的故障與錯誤。
本公司依賴第三方提供業務基礎設施的關鍵零組件。
本公司採用以關係為基礎的運營模式，維護本公司聲譽的能力對業務成功至關重要，未能做到可能會對本公司表現造成重大不利影響。
本公司可能因其他金融機構或市場機構的財務狀況不佳而受到不利影響。
近年來外部與內部風險已大幅增加。
本公司風險管理架構可能無法有效降低對本公司而言的風險及/或損失。
系統故障或網路安全遭入侵，包括因網路攻擊或資料安全事件所致，可能使本公司面臨增加的運營成本以及訴訟及其他負債。
本公司業務連續性計畫或資料安全系統可能不足，導致業務出現重大中斷或幹擾，並對營運成果造成負面影響。
本公司依賴資料與模型的應用，不僅在管理層的決策中，也在符合監管預期方面尤為重要。
本公司可能面臨因取得產權而產生環境責任風險。
與我們監管環境相關之風險
本公司所屬產業受高度規範，且監管架構，加上未來任何立法或監管變動，可能對本公司營運產生重大不利影響。
本公司需遵守嚴格的資本要求，此等要求可能對本公司營運產生不利影響。
paragraphs: 除本年度報告表10-K中所載其他資訊，包括「對未來預測陳述之警示說明」及「管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之分析」，以及我們合併財務報表與相關附註資訊外，您應謹慎考量下列因素。這些因素可能對我們未來之業務、財務狀況、流動性及營運結果產生不利影響，並可能導致我們實際結果與歷史結果或本年度報告表10-K中所含未來預測陳述之結果有重大差異，進而使我們普通股之交易價格下跌。我們之業務、財務狀況、流動性或營運結果亦可能因目前未為我們所知或我們目前認為非重大之風險與不確定性而受到損害。本風險因素中提及之過去事件僅為範例，並非完整清單，亦非表示這些因素是否曾於過去發生或未來發生之可能性。

我們之業務取決於我們能否成功衡量並管理信用風險。作為貸款人，我們面臨貸款本金或利息未能按時或完全償還之風險，或擔保貸款之價值不足以覆蓋我們之敞口。此外，我們亦面臨貸款償還期間之風險、貸款審核之風險、經濟與產業條件變動之風險，以及處理個別貸款與借款人之內在風險。借款人的信用worthiness受許多因素影響，包括地方市場條件與總體經濟條件。我們許多貸款是提供給規模較小至中型企業，這些企業較難承受競爭、經濟與財務壓力。若美國總體經濟氣候，或我們特定市場，遭遇重大幹擾，借款人可能面臨償還貸款之困難，我們所持有之擔保品可能價值下降或變得不易變現，非 Performing貸款、核銷與逾期貸款之數量可能增加，並需要增加貸款信用損失之備抵提列。與多戶住宅貸款、不動產建設及其他商業不動產貸款之信用品質相關之其他因素包括企業管理品質與租賃空置率。

我們之風險管理作法，例如監測貸款在特定市場之集中度與信用批准、審查與行政作業，可能無法充分降低信用風險，且我們之信用行政人員、政策與程序可能無法適應影響客戶與貸款組合品質之經濟或其他條件變動。未能有效衡量並控制貸款組合之信用風險，可能導致貸款違約、拍賣與增加核銷，並可能迫使我們大幅提高貸款信用損失之備抵提列，這將對我們之淨收入產生不利影響。因此，我們未能成功管理信用風險，可能對我們之業務、財務狀況與營運結果產生不利影響。

銀行業經驗顯示，我們之貸款中將有一部分會逾期，且部分貸款可能僅部分償還或完全無法償還。我們可能因超出我們控制範圍之原因而遭受損失，例如總體經濟條件對客戶及其業務之影響。因此，我們維持貸款信用損失備抵提列，以反映管理階層對貸款組閤中預期損失與內在風險之判斷。在決定貸款信用損失備抵提列之規模時，我們依賴對貸款組合之分析，考量歷史損失經驗、貸款數量與類型、分類趨勢、逾期與非應計貸款之數量與趨勢、經濟條件及其他相關資訊。確定貸款信用損失備抵提列適當水準之過程具有高度主觀性，並要求我們根據適用之評估日期所存在之因素與情況，使用重大判斷力來估計機構之信用風險與預期損失水準，所有這些因素都可能有重大變動。儘管我們努力維持貸款信用損失備抵提列於足以吸收貸款組閤中任何內在預期損失之水準，但這些貸款信用損失之估計值
貸款信用減損係屬主觀性，其準確性取決於未來事件的結果。截至2025年12月31日，貸款信用減損備抵額為19.8 百萬美元，或總貸款餘額的1.00%，扣除未實現收入後計算。
影響借款人之經濟條件惡化、有關現有貸款之新資訊、錯誤之管理假設、發現更多問題貸款、暫時性調整、貸款豁免、自動緩償及其他因素，無論是否在我們控制範圍內，都可能導致我們面臨更高水平之非 Performing資產與核銷，並產生超過目前貸款信用損失備抵提列之貸款信用損失，迫使我們做出重大增加貸款信用損失備抵提列之調整，這可能對我們之業務、財務狀況與營運結果產生不利影響。
